test_title: PYST 1: SSC Stenographer - English (Held on: 11 Nov 2021 Shift 1 )
subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. **

Are you trying to say that you are stupid __so__ proud of it?
solution:
The correct answer is: **but**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace **'so' **with **'but' **to make the sentence correct.
 
• We use **so **as a subordinating conjunction to introduce clauses of result or decision.
 
 
• **Example -*** I got here late. It was a long journey, **so **I'm really tired now.*
 
 
 
• **But** is used to introduce an added statement, usually something that is different from what you have said before.
 
 
• **Example -** *She's very hard-working **but **not very imaginative.*
 
 
 
• So, according to the given sentence, **one cannot be stupid and proud of his/her stupidity at the same time. But is used to connect ideas that contrast.**

Hence, **option 4** is the appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment.

**Improved sentence:** *Are you trying to say that you are stupid but__ proud of it?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• We use **so that** in order that to talk about purpose. We often use them with modal verbs (can, would, will, etc.).
 
• We often use** though** to introduce a fact which you regard as less important than the fact in the main clause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• **“But”** indicates a complete negation and is usually used after a comma, in the middle of a sentence.
 
• **“Though”** is usually used at the end of a sentence and indicates a partial negation.
